findings.evidence: Section 3 "Recognition names the behavior and its effect, then stops" and Section 6 "The recipient of feedback can send the same recap" restate generic feedback advice the model already knows; the SBI skeleton itself is well known.
findings.fix: Trim the generic restatements. Keep the dispute test, the thin-evidence placeholder default, the rule that Rule 1 separates praise from correction, and the leave-out-silently confidentiality rule.

findings.evidence: One file mixes a routing table (Section 2, with Rules 1-6 under it), a delivery procedure, a receiving flow, an expectation-reset flow and a recap. It reads as a Process skill with Navigation traits and no single clear shape. Section 4 and Section 5 give a thinking test only for receiving, while the reset rules are a bullet list.
findings.fix: Add a short "before you reset expectations, ask: ..." test to Section 5, like the dispute test in Section 3 and the instance-or-label test in Section 4. Number the Rules as a separate list from the Sections so "Rule 3" and "Section 4" are not both references into the same document.

findings.evidence: The Gotchas section is strong with reasons, but its items are not tied back to where they apply. For example the "never deliver right before the person presents" gotcha has no eval and no pre-send gate check.
findings.fix: Add the timing check (before a presentation, demo or on-call shift) to the Section 3 pre-send gate, so the highest-consequence gotchas are enforced where drafts are finalized.

findings.evidence: description: "Prepare, deliver, receive and follow up on specific workplace feedback using Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI)... Not for ... (use difficult-workplace-conversations)." There are no tool or format keywords such as 1:1, recap, or stakeholder pushback phrased as user intent. The routing hint for impression-only or hearsay cases is missing.
findings.fix: Prepare, deliver, receive and follow up on specific workplace feedback with Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI), and reset stakeholder expectations with explicit scope/date trade-offs. Use when thanking a teammate for specific work, raising an observable behavior (broken builds, missed commitments, interrupting), answering vague criticism such as "you're unreliable", turning notes or a vibe about a report into a 1:1 talking point, prepping upward feedback, giving feedback to two people in a conflict you lead, writing the follow-up recap, or pushing back on a deadline or scope creep, even if the user never says feedback. Not for ceremonial congratulations (work anniversaries, birthdays, farewells), legal or HR determinations, PIPs, ratings, policy drafting, or layoffs and salary talks (use difficult-workplace-conversations).

findings.evidence: The Section 2 table gates references with conditions ("only if evidence is disputed..."). However, Section 5 lists "Load: expectation-alignment.md for sample dialogue, the scope-change template, or an ownership reset" without naming when not to load it. Section 5's inline reset rules already cover simple deadline pushback.
findings.fix: State in the table that simple deadline or scope pushback with a feasible option needs no load of expectation-alignment.md. Load it only for a scope-change template, an ownership reset, or multi-party dialogue.

findings.evidence: Section 5 leaves the user choosing their own phrasing for most steps, while the "Rule 1... never in the same conversation or message" ban on mixed praise and correction is stated rigidly. No escape hatch is given for a user who explicitly insists on a combined message.
findings.fix: Add one line saying what to do when the user insists on combining praise and correction: draft them as two separate messages and explain why in one sentence.

findings.evidence: There are 11 evals with verifiable assertions, but none covers Rule 1 (mixed recognition and correction request) or Rule 6 (formal matters such as harassment or safety). The ownership-reset eval's file points to references/expectation-alignment.md rather than an input in evals/files/. The trigger set has 10 positives and 9 negatives. Most positives name the domain explicitly, and no should-trigger query covers an indirect case such as the Section 5 "add people" objection.
findings.fix: Add one eval for a mixed praise-plus-criticism request and one for a harassment disclosure. Move the ownership-reset input into evals/files/. Add one more should-not-trigger near-miss and one should-trigger query without the word feedback or 1:1.

findings.evidence: Section 2 routes to "Rule 1-6" and "Section 4/5", but the Rules are a numbered list below the table and the Sections are headings, so both use the same numbers. The hearsay or third-party-report branch loads feedback-sbi-model.md but gives no inline instruction on what to do with the hearsay. The exit for "user cannot name any instance" is stated only in Section 1.
findings.fix: Rename the list "Rules R1-R6" and refer to them as R1..R6 in the table. Add an inline line for the third-party-report case: use only the user's own observed instance and never name the reporter.
